content: 1. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Conversely, fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Both fluphenazine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 3. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate enhances the effects of fondaparinux by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 4. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and formoterol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosamprenavir also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate also increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 7. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Both gemifloxacin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 9. Both gilteritinib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 10. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and givinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 11. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and glasdegib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc prolongation. 12. Both granisetron and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Both haloperidol and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate enhances the effects of heparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 17. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Both hydroxychloroquine sulfate and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 21. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both imipramine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 24. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 26. Both inotuzumab and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation of any QTc-prolonging drug, and monitor periodically as clinically indicated during treatment. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 28. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Both isoflurane and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 30. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 31. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both itraconazole and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Both ivosidenib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect of these drugs. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 35. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lapatinib also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Lasmiditan increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 38. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 39. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 40. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and levoketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 41. Both lithium and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 42. Both lofepramine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 43. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 44. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 45. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 48. Both macimorelin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 ms in the corrected QT interval. Avoid coadministration with drugs that prolong the QT interval, as this could increase the risk of torsade de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 49. Both maprotiline and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 51. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 53. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 55. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 56. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of microbiota oral therapy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Microbiota oral contains bacterial spores, and antibacterial agents may reduce its efficacy if coadministered. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 58. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 59. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of midazolam intranasal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Coadministration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with midazolam intranasal causes higher systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. 60. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 61. Both mirtazapine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 62. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of mizolastine by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 63. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and moxifloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 64. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 65. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 66. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 67. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nelfinavir also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 68. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 69. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 70. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 71. Nifedipine increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 72. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and nilotinib prolong the QTc interval. Nilotinib also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 73. Nilutamide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 74. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 75. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 76. Both nortriptyline and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs.
